did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah received the word of the LORD a second time while he was confined in the courtyard of the guard—even during imprisonment and siege, prophetic revelation continued to come to him.
Did you know? The LORD invites Jeremiah to call on him and promises to answer him and reveal great and hidden things to him—things he had not known before.
Did you know? Alongside the description of destruction, the LORD promises Jerusalem restoration, healing, forgiveness, and an abundance of peace and truth.
Did you know? The prophecy describes a complete transformation in Jerusalem and the cities of Judah: from desolate places empty of people and animals into places where life will return.
Did you know? The expected sounds of restoration include rejoicing and gladness, the voices of bridegroom and bride, and thanksgiving to the LORD in the Temple.

Did you know? The restoration is not limited to Jerusalem: it includes the cities of the hill country, the foothills, and the Negev, the land of Benjamin, and the cities of Judah, where flocks will once again pass under the hand of the one who counts them.
Did you know? The LORD promises to make a righteous Branch sprout for David—a ruler who will carry out justice and righteousness in the land.
Did you know? As part of the promise of restoration, Judah will be saved, Jerusalem will live in safety, and the city will be called “The LORD Is Our Righteousness.”
Did you know? The covenant with David and the Levites is compared to the fixed order of day and night: only if their regular pattern could be broken would the covenant also be broken.
Did you know? The number of David’s descendants and the Levites is described using two vast images from nature: the host of heaven and the sand of the sea.
